children.text:
G'day! Navigating healthcare in Australia is simple once you know the golden rules:

• *Rule 1: GP First:* A General Practitioner (GP) is your primary doctor for non-emergencies, prescriptions, and official uni sick certificates.

• *Rule 2: Direct Billing is Magic:* Choose a clinic in your OSHC insurer’s network that does "direct billing". They bill your insurer directly so you pay $0 upfront!

• *Rule 3: Need a Specialist?* Want to see a dermatologist or specialist? You MUST get a referral letter from your GP first to ensure your OSHC covers it.

• *Rule 4: Emergencies:* Call 000 only for serious, life-threatening emergencies.
You have had a persistent sore throat, mild fever, and tiredness for four days. You want medical advice, but it is not an emergency. What is generally the most appropriate first step?

children.text:
*Correct Answer:* Option B (Book an appointment with a General Practitioner (GP))

💡 *Explanation:* In Australia, a General Practitioner (GP) is generally your primary healthcare contact for non-emergency illnesses. Emergency departments and 000 ambulances are reserved for life-threatening medical situations.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What to do if you get sick in Australia](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/

*Correct Answer:* Option B (Consult a GP first to obtain an official referral letter)

💡 *Explanation:* In Australia, specialist consultations generally require a referral letter from a GP. Without a valid referral, your OSHC insurer may not pay benefits for the specialist appointment.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What you need to know about the Australian healthcare system](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/understanding-australian-healthcare/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/understanding-australian-healthcare/

*Correct Answer:* Option A (A medical practice in your OSHC insurer’s direct billing network)

💡 *Explanation:* Direct billing network clinics have agreements with your OSHC provider to send the medical bill directly to the insurer. This helps reduce or eliminate the upfront payment you need to make at the time of your visit.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What to do if you get sick in Australia](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/

*Correct Answer:* Option A (Online Doctor consultations for 24/7 video or phone appointments)

💡 *Explanation:* Many OSHC apps offer a 24/7 Online Doctor service where students can speak with qualified doctors via video or phone for medical advice, prescriptions, and certificates with no out-of-pocket costs.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) | Overseas | Medibank](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/oshc/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/oshc/

*Correct Answer:* Option A (The National Health Services Directory via Healthdirect or your OSHC provider)

💡 *Explanation:* You can find accredited general practices and medical clinics using the Australian Government’s Healthdirect directory or the provider search tool on your OSHC insurer’s website and app.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What to do if you get sick in Australia](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/

• *Healthdirect Hotline:* 1800 022 222 (24/7 Registered Nurse advice)
• *Emergency Services:* 000 (Ambulance, Fire, Police - life threats only)
• *National Home Doctor:* 13 74 25 (After-hours bulk-billed home visits)
